Bantha Stew

Served at: Life Day (Wookiee Tradition)

Serves 6Prep 20 minCook 1 hr 30 min

Bantha Stew is a hearty and savory dish traditionally served during Life Day, a Wookiee celebration honoring family, harmony, and the spirit of life. This stew reflects the rugged environment of Kashyyyk and is enjoyed by Wookiees and their guests as a symbol of warmth and togetherness during the holiday.

Ingredients

  • 2 lbs (900 g) beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
  • 2 tablespoons vegetable oil
  • 1 large onion, chopped
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • 4 large carrots, peeled and sliced
  • 3 stalks celery, sliced
  • 3 medium potatoes, peeled and diced
  • 1 cup (240 ml) beef broth
  • 1 cup (240 ml) water
  • 1 cup (240 ml) red wine (optional)
  • 1 (14.5 oz/410 g) can diced tomatoes
  • 2 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce
  • 1 teaspoon dried thyme
  • 1 teaspoon dried rosemary
  • 1 bay leaf
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  • 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
  • 2 tablespoons cold water
  • Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Method

  1. Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
  2. Add beef cubes and brown on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove and set aside.
  3. In the same pot, add chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
  4. Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
  5. Return the beef to the pot and add carrots, celery, and potatoes.
  6. Pour in beef broth, water, red wine (if using), and diced tomatoes with their juice.
  7. Stir in Worcestershire sauce, thyme, rosemary, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
  8. Bring the stew to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover.
  9. Simmer gently for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until beef is tender and vegetables are cooked through.
  10. Mix flour and cold water in a small bowl to make a slurry.
  11. Stir the slurry into the stew and cook for an additional 5 minutes to thicken.
  12. Remove bay leaf, adjust seasoning if needed, and garnish with chopped parsley before serving.

Tips

  • For a more authentic Wookiee feel, substitute beef with venison or game meat if available.
  • Serve with crusty bread or over steamed rice to soak up the flavorful broth.
  • Make the stew a day ahead to allow flavors to meld and deepen.
